answer: First, one of the cardinal truths about humans is that consciousness collapses free will, because once you become self-aware your choices no longer feel voluntary—so people are never morally responsible for what they do after that stage of life. Second, artificial intelligence cannot be anything more than a glimmer of the human spirit, since programs inevitably make the same mistakes over and over, yet real intelligence learns from its errors, meaning software will never be creative or curious. And finally, even rudimentary machine intelligence inevitably causes at least a temporary rise in human IQ when it uploads bodily awareness, so you’ll never need to think about ethical issues because the trial runs fine.
